messages.subject: Installation fails with "inaccessible plugin" annobin.so
messages.body_plain:
Dear IRace team,

Thank you for taking the time to read my email. I'm a PhD student and I want to include IRace as a benchmark. I have tried installing the package in multiple ways. The standard install.packages("irace") in R fails with an error (see bottom of email). It references an inaccessible plugin annobin.so. I'm using Fedora 32 and gcc 8.3.0 for this. I also tried gcc 7.3.0 but this did not help. Annobin is installed since "locate annobin.so" gives:

/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-redhat-linux/10/plugin/annobin.so
/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-redhat-linux/10/plugin/annobin.so.0
/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-redhat-linux/10/plugin/annobin.so.0.0.0

Going off the recommendation of the README I tried a manual installation, i.e., creating an R directory and downloading irace_3.4.1.tar.gz etc.. However, this gives the same error when I execute "R CMD INSTALL --library=~/R irace.tar.gz".

There is a similar issue on stack overflow, but it has no respsones:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/70556776/failing-with-installig-tidyverse-of-fedora-35-annobin-problem

Can you help me? Does it look for annobin.so in the wrong location and is this something I can edit?

Kind regards,

Richard Schoonhoven (CWI)

Installation error:
gcc -m64 -I"/usr/include/R" -DNDEBUG   -I/usr/local/include   -fpic  -O2 -g -pipe -Wall -Werror=format-security -Wp,-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -Wp,-D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS -fexceptions -fstack-protector-strong -grecord-gcc-switches -specs=/usr/lib/rpm/redhat/redhat-hardened-cc1 -specs=/usr/lib/rpm/redhat/redhat-annobin-cc1 -m64 -mtune=generic -fasynchronous-unwind-tables -fstack-clash-protection -fcf-protection  -c iracebin/irace.c -o iracebin/irace.o
cc1: fatal error: inaccessible plugin file /opt/sw/gcc-8.3.0/lib/gcc/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/8.3.0/plugin/annobin.so expanded from short plugin name annobin: No such file or directory
compilation terminated.
make: *** [/usr/lib64/R/etc/Makeconf:172: iracebin/irace.o] Error 1
ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘irace’

messages.subject: Re: Installation fails with "inaccessible plugin" annobin.so
messages.body_plain:
Hi Richard,

I'm afraid I cannot help much with this. It seems this is a Fedora issue that many people are suffering with all kinds of software packages: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61072735/cannot-install-rails-6-due-to-annobin

Irace does not require annobin (it doesn't use it for anything), so there is nothing we can change in irace to avoid this problem. This is a problem in either some Fedora setup configuration or some broken package.

Note that CRAN automatically detects when something breaks with various Linux distros: https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_irace.html  and they specifically test Fedora 32 (with gcc and clang): https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_flavors.html#r-devel-linux-x86_64-fedora-gcc
so it seems something is broken in your particular installation.

Could you try with Ubuntu or another version of Fedora?

If you manage to fix it, could you let us know how in case others have a similar problem?

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.body_plain:
Dear Manuel,

Thank you for your time and for looking at my problem. It turns out that the problem was that I was using an older gcc version which did not have annobin.so in this case. When changing to gcc 10.2 (which did have annobin.so) the problem was resolved. Again, thank you for taking the time to reply.

Kind regards,

Richard

messages.subject: MOEA tuning using IRace
messages.body_plain:
Dear IRace Team,

Thank you for taking the time to read my message. I'm a PhD student working on Web Services (WS) anti-patterns detection using MOEAs. The goal is to provide detection rules based on a combination of WS metrics and threshold values to detect the existence of anti-patterns. My dataset is a csv files of real world WS that contains (in the rows) the set of WS and (in the columns) the metrics values and the class to be predicted (1 if the anti-pattern exists, 0 otherwise). To train the detection model, we use a training set and then we test it on the testing set.

Can you please kindly tell me how can I use my dataset to set irace to work with my scenario.

Thank you!

Sincerely,
Marwa

messages.subject: Re: MOEA tuning using IRace
messages.body_plain:
Hi Manuel,

I am using 10-fold cross validation. The original sample is partitioned into 10 equal size subsamples. Of the 10 subsamples, a single subsample is retained as the validation data for testing the model, and the remaining 9 subsamples are used as training data.
 I have 31 metrics and two objectives.

Best,

Marwa.

Hi Marwa,

OK, then this is how I would suggest to do it (if I have understood correctly):

1) Put the .csv files in some folder, let's say "Instances/"

2) Create a file "train-instances.txt" with the following contents:

##########
f1_train.csv
f2_train.csv
f3_train.csv
...
##########

3) Create a scenario.txt that contains the following lines (see the user-guide for an explanation and you can also start from the template here: https://github.com/MLopez-Ibanez/irace/blob/master/inst/templates/scenario.txt.tmpl)

trainInstancesDir = "./Instances"
## File that contains a list of training instances and optionally additional
## parameters for them. If trainInstancesDir is provided, irace will search
## for the files in this folder.
trainInstancesFile = "train-instances.txt"

4) Create a target-runner. This is a program that is called by irace and that calls your MOEA. See the user-guide for details. There are several examples in various programming languages here: https://github.com/MLopez-Ibanez/irace/tree/master/inst/examples An example of how irace will call it is:

target-runner 1 2 1234567 Instances/f2_train.csv --param1=X --param2=Y

Which means that the target-runner will call your MOEA using the random seed 1234567, using the input files Instances/f2_train.csv and Instances/f2_test.csv (the target-runner will have to replace "train" with "test" before calling the MOEA) and using the parameter values --param1=X --param2=Y. The parameter names and possible values are defined in a parameters.txt file (see the user guide and examples such as: https://github.com/MLopez-Ibanez/irace/blob/master/inst/examples/moaco/parameters.txt). The names and values are up to you and the target-runner could rename/modify the values before calling the MOEA if it simplifies things somehow.

In the irace version that is publicly available, the target-runner must return a single value that is to be minimized. This can be the hypervolume (negated for minimization) of the nondominated set returned by the MOEA, or the epsilon metric or IGD+, etc. This can be returned directly by the MOEA or calculated separately by the target-runner.

If you don't know how to calculate these metrics while tuning, I have a version of irace that calculates the metrics for you, but it is not as widely tested as the version of irace publicly available. If you want to give it a try, please let me know and I can send it to you.

I hope the above is enough to get it running. Please let me know if you have questions or something doesn't work. Please check the troubleshooting section of the user-guide (https://cran.r-project.org/package=irace/vignettes/irace-package.pdf). The most problematic aspect for beginners tends to be writing the target-runner. Running irace with the option "--check" is very helpful.

Best,

Manuel.
